title: Google launches Momentum initiative to support India's AI startups with technology, infrastructure and scale
summary: Google launches Momentum initiative to support Indian AI startups with infrastructure
detailed: Google has introduced Momentum, a new initiative aimed at supporting India's startup ecosystem with technology, engineering expertise, infrastructure and access to customers as artificial intelligence (AI) accelerates product development and changes the way businesses scale.
Google said its support for startups will extend beyond technology to infrastructure costs, customer acquisition, security and market expansion.

It cited Phot.ai as an example of a startup that has integrated Google's image-generation technology into its creative platform, while using Google Cloud to scale its AI infrastructure and reduce inference costs.

Google is also supporting startups working on scientific and environmental challenges through the AI for the Planet Accelerator, an initiative by Google DeepMind that provides access to frontier AI technology and technical expertise for applications in climate, agriculture and environmental resilience.
sentences: Google has introduced Momentum, a new initiative aimed at supporting India's startup ecosystem with technology, engineering expertise, infrastructure and access to customers as artificial intelligence (AI) accelerates product development and changes the way businesses scale.
The initiative builds on Google's decade-long engagement with Indian startups through its Google for Startups Accelerator programmes.
It will focus on helping founders move beyond product development to areas such as trusted AI deployment, customer acquisition, commercial readiness and expansion into new markets.
In a blog post, Google said AI is making it faster for startups to turn ideas into products, but is also raising expectations around building sustainable businesses.
Momentum is intended to bring more of Google's technology and resources to Indian founders across different stages of growth.

AI startups report gains in efficiency and product development
Healthcare technology startup AiSteth has screened more than 160,000 patients across over 20 Indian states.
Through Google's AI First accelerator programme, it developed an offline-capable, edge-encrypted minimum viable product (MVP) for cardiac screening.
The company is also using Google's Gemini, MedGemma and Gemma models for clinical summaries and personalised auscultation training.
Legal-tech startup SpotDraft has integrated Gemini with on-device capabilities through Chrome to improve its AI-powered contract workflows.
The integration has helped reduce latency by 70% and processing costs by 80%, while improving accuracy on its challenge dataset, Google said.
VideoSDK, meanwhile, has built real-time conversational AI agents using the Gemini Live API, reporting a 25% improvement in response quality.
Its use of Google Cloud has also helped reduce infrastructure costs by around 40%.
The initiative also focuses on supporting the development of AI capabilities suited to India's linguistic and business requirements.
Google cited Shunya Labs, which is developing enterprise AI products across voice technology, small language models and reasoning systems.
Its technology supports more than 200 languages and dialects and draws on open resources such as Project Vaani speech data and Google's Gemma models.
Its Hindi speech-recognition model can operate offline, while its conversational routing technology can be deployed within a customer's own premises.
Another startup, ZenteiQ, spun out of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, is developing smaller AI models designed to run on edge devices.
The company used Google Cloud TPUs to train models and Google Kubernetes Engine to scale synthetic-data generation, increasing overall inference throughput fourfold.
ZenteiQ has also been selected under the IndiaAI Mission to develop indigenous foundation models across English and 10 Indian languages, according to Google.
Google said its support for startups will extend beyond technology to infrastructure costs, customer acquisition, security and market expansion.

It cited Phot.ai as an example of a startup that has integrated Google's image-generation technology into its creative platform, while using Google Cloud to scale its AI infrastructure and reduce inference costs.
The company has also worked with Google Ads specialists to strengthen customer acquisition across markets.

Google is also supporting startups working on scientific and environmental challenges through the AI for the Planet Accelerator, an initiative by Google DeepMind that provides access to frontier AI technology and technical expertise for applications in climate, agriculture and environmental resilience.
The company said security, privacy and responsible AI development would remain central to its support as Indian startups move towards wider adoption and deployment.
